Abstract 26

Background/objective: The novel coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic poses a 27

global threat to the public health. There is a challenge in measuring the patient’s length of 28

hospital stay and managing the healthcare resources to handle the situation successfully. Our 29

objective is to use the qPCR cycle of threshold (Ct) as a tool in evaluating the severity of the 30

infection and hence the length of hospital stay to better utilize and manage the healthcare 31

resources. 32

Methods: This cross sectional study was carried out on 306 patients who admitted to COVID-19 33

care centers in Kingdom of Bahrain from 20th March 2020 to 5th April 2020. Standard qPCR was 34

used to  estimate the viral load  and data were analyzed to investigate the relationship between Ct 35

values and various variables. 36

Results: Out of 306 patients, 2 deaths, 1 active stable case and 303 recovered cases were 37

reported. Ct value was significantly and negatively associated (P value <0.001) with length of 38

hospital stay. The viral clearance was also inversely associated with the Ct values. 39

Conclusion: Ct value was inversely associated with hospital stay duration (and time to viral 40

clearance), higher the Ct value is indicative of faster time to viral clearance. This association 41

could help to better manage the infection and resources allocation. 42

Keywords: COVID-19; SARS-CoV-2; cycle of threshold; viral clearance; length of hospital stay 43

Introduction 52

Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is caused by the newly identified strain of the 53

Coronavirus family Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) 1. Whilst 54

some patients may have mild symptoms, others develop a severe respiratory distress syndrome 55

with features of a blood coagulopathy requiring intensive support 2. As a result, COVID-19 has 56

rapidly evolved into a pandemic that has put a severe burden on the healthcare services of some 57

countries, notably beds for both hospitalization and intensive care facilities 3. Testing aids case 58

identification, case isolation and contact tracing, all of which are vital to limit coronavirus spread 59

4.  Currently, the main diagnostic test for SARS-CoV-2 is the real-time Reverse Transcription 60

Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) 5.The RT-PCR result is influenced by the Cycle 61

Threshold (Ct-Value) that has been suggested as a quantitative test to indirectly assess the viral 62

load 6 with severe cases having a much higher viral load than mild cases 7. Therefore, the aim of 63

this study was to measure the viral load determined by the Ct value and relate that to viral 64

clearance to determine if this could predict length of hospital stay, as that may help guide 65

healthcare resource allocation. 66

Methods 67

Patients and Sample Collection 68

A cross sectional study was undertaken on 306 patients who were admitted to COVID-19 care 69

centers in the Kingdom of Bahrain between March 20th, 2020 and April 5th, 2020. Of those 306 70

patients, 303 had recovered from their COVID-19 disease. Data were recorded for 71

demographics, Ct-value on admission, time to viral clearance, and data on the length of stay and 72

patient outcomes. At the time of the study, the local protocol in Bahrain admits all positive cases 73

to treatment/isolation facilities regardless of being symptomatic or asymptomatic. The patients 74

are discharged when they have two negative nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs on two 75

consecutive days. All admitted patients are tested after three days of being asymptomatic and, if 76

negative, the test is repeated after 24 hours to confirm viral clearance, following which the 77

patients are discharged. Therefore, the length of stay was the same as the time to viral clearance 78

and the minimum stay of patients is four days. 79

RNA Extraction and SARS-Cov-2 RNA Amplification 81

The diagnostic test used for SARS-CoV-2 was performed using qPCR on nasopharyngeal and 82

oropharyngeal samples. The samples were transferred to a viral transport media immediately 83

after collection and transported to a COVID-19 laboratory for testing. Diagnosed cases were a 84

heterogeneous sample of tested patients, they included symptomatic and asymptomatic 85

individuals with recent exposure to a confirmed COVID19 case or travelers arriving from high 86

risk countries. PCR test was conducted using Thermo Fisher Scientific (Waltham, MA) TaqPath 87

1-Step RT-qPCR Master Mix, CG on the Applied Biosystems (Foster City, CA) 7500 Fast Dx 88

RealTime PCR Instrument. The assay used followed the WHO protocol from Charité Virology, 89

Berlin, Germany 8. and targeted the E gene. If the E gene was detected, the sample was then 90

confirmed by RdRP and N genes. The E gene CT value was reported and used in this study. CT 91

Values >40 were considered negative. Positive and negative controls were included  for quality 92

control purposes. 93

RT-qPCR Analytical Validation 94

Linear range was determined using serial log10 dilutions of standard RNA and was established 95

between 3·5 x 103 to 3·5 x 1012 copies of RNA/mL, with amplification efficiency of 87% and 96

with a regression R2 value higher than 0.99. 97

Statistical Analysis 98

Categorical parameters were expressed as frequencies (%), whereas continuous variables are 99

presented as mean. Data trends were visually and statistically evaluated for normality. We used 100

regression analysis to describe the relationship between categorical variables and between 101

continuous variables with the main outcome. Two-way Student’s t test was then used to detect 102

the difference between Ct values across symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. Statistical 103

analysis was performed using STATA statistical computer package (StataCorp. 2013. Stata 104

Statistical Software). 105

Results 116

Of the 306 patients, there were 303 who had recovered, whilst 2 deaths and 1 active stable case 117

were excluded from the analysis. 118

The descriptive summary of the patients is shown in Table 1. The sample of patients included 119

cases who arrived in Bahrain from other countries, all travelers being tested upon arrival, and 120

included cases of local spread. Initially, gender distribution of COVID-19 cases in Bahrain was 121

equal; however, as the infection started to spread within the community of labor workers, who 122

are mainly males, the ratio of males to females and the ratio of local cases to cases coming from 123

other countries increased.  Symptomatic patients were 12.2% of the sample, which corresponded 124

to a similar percentage of the symptomatic patients in the entire population. 125

Ct values showed a statistically significant negative correlation of 0.28 with the length of 126

hospital stay and time to viral clearance as seen in Figure 1 showing the Lowess smoothing curve 127

of hospital stay. Higher Ct values on admission predicted shorter hospital stays and shorter time 128

to clear the virus. The regression analysis showed similar results when using a univariate 129

analysis and a multivariate analysis adjusted for age and gender. Ct value had a significant 130

inverse correlation with the length of stay, 10 points higher on the Ct value correlating with a 131

shorter hospital stay of 2.8 days. 132

Patients with high Ct values defined as ≥35 had shorter hospital stays, by 4.3 days, when 133

compared to patients with Ct values <35 on admission. 134

The regression analysis for Length of Stay using Ct value as a covariate is shown in Table 2. 135

Analysis on symptomatic individuals showed that symptomatic individuals have a lower mean Ct 136

value when compared to asymptomatic individuals. Asymptomatic individuals had a mean Ct 137

Discussion 141

This study has shown that the higher the Ct values, the more rapid the viral clearance, leading to 142

a shorter length of stay in hospital. A Ct value >35 predicted a shorter hospital stay by 4.3 days, 143

and a 10 unit increase in Ct value was associated with a shortened time to viral clearance of 2.8 144

days. Ct values have been reported as an indirect assessment of the viral load 6, 7, with higher Ct 145

values having a lower viral load, and it has been shown that those patients with more severe 146

disease have lower Ct values 7. Higher Ct values indicate an early infection or a recovering 147

infection. Whilst Ct values can be used to predict length of hospital stay for stable cases, the Ct 148

value cannot, however, predict outcomes. Outcomes are influenced by many additional 149

predictors, most notably comorbidities and severity of disease 9. The presence of age greater than 150

60 and comorbidities including diabetes, hypertension, obesity and respiratory disease may offset 151

a high Ct values and further studies to predict outcomes based on Ct value taking into account 152

adverse risk factors of disease severity are needed. 153

In this study, symptomatic individuals had lower Ct values whilst asymptomatic individuals had 154

higher Ct values, suggesting that the lower Ct values reflects a more severe presentation. 155

However, asymptomatic individuals still had a low mean Ct values  (27.8) indicating a 156

significant viral load, suggesting that asymptomatic individuals can still transmit the disease 10. 157

These results are in accord with those of Liu et al who reported that the mean viral load of severe 158

cases was around 60 times higher than that of mild cases 7. La Scola et. al have reported using 159

cell culture system that patients with Ct values >= 34 do not shed infectious virions, and hence 160

are not infectious and can be discharged from hospitals  or care centers11 . 161

Bahrain has pursued a comprehensive testing program with all travelers arriving in the country 162

being tested, mobile screening services, random screening in high risk communities and 163

extensive contact tracing. This strategy has resulted in detecting many asymptomatic patients, in 164

contrast to other countries where the response has been directed solely towards symptomatic 165

patients, and has generated data that is critical for production of accurate prediction models 12. 166

Limitations of this study include that it was cross sectional and that the number of symptomatic 167

cases were few in number. The number of patients with multiple comorbidities were few and 168

therefore a model to take into account the protective effect of a high Ct value could not be 169

determined. 170

Conclusion 171

In this current study it was evident that Ct value can predict the duration of hospital stay of 172

COVID-19 infected patients, which also suggests that viral clearance will be faster in higher Ct 173

value patients. This data can be implemented in other country to evaluate the patients stay at 174

hospital and also helpful in managing the healthcare staff in successfully handling the COVID- 175

19 infected patients. 176
